Broken Heart Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Broken Heart because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+1F494, which you can use as 💔 in HTML, \01F494 in CSS, but the Alt+decimal method does not work because the codepoint is above the Basic Multilingual Plane. If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Copy the Broken Heart character from this page when you need it in a form, chat message or document that does not accept Alt codes. Broken Heart has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape 💔 or the hex escape 💔.

How to type broken heart on Windows

  1. Broken Heart cannot be typed with a legacy Alt code or Alt + decimal because its codepoint is above U+FFFF.
  2. Use the Character Viewer, an HTML entity, or copy the character directly.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type broken heart on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Broken Heart. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Broken Heart" and click the character to insert it.

How to use broken heart in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\01F494"; ()
  • Python: \U0001F494 or chr(0x1F494)
  • JavaScript: \u{1F494} or String.fromCodePoint(0x1F494)
  • JSON: "\uD83D\uDC94" (surrogate pair)

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for 💔?

No legacy Alt code exists for Broken Heart because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+1F494 in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type 💔 without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as 💔, or copy the character directly from this page.

What is the Unicode for Broken Heart?

The Unicode codepoint for Broken Heart is U+1F494. You can use this value in HTML as 💔, in CSS as \01F494, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type 💔 on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+1F494, then click it.
